published_source: Printed Table 1 of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.4716.pdf), read Nov 4; earlier values were the log's rounded ones (0.5, 0.05) (PROTOCOL ruling (f)).
replication_status: approximate (random_subsample: the authors' plm code and fixest agree to 1e-12 on the shipped sample; full-panel coefficient not reproducible from shipped data; subsample TWFE 0.4942 vs published 0.5, -1.2% and z = -0.06 in subsample SEs)
notes: Unal and Park (2023), one-click buying adoption. Outcome MonthlyFrequency = online orders placed per customer-month, levels (no log). Authors' code (Table1.R line 42): plm(MonthlyFrequency ~ factor(month) + postentry, index = 'customer', model = 'within') on the full unmatched panel, i.e. customer FE + 34 month dummies, no controls, no weights; SE vcovHC(HC0, cluster = 'group') times the Stata-style factor (G/(G-1))(N-1)/df.residual with df.residual = N - G - 35 (fixest's default ssc gives SEs 1.5% smaller; same point estimate). Treatment postentry = 1[month >= entry] for adopters (verified row by row), 0 in every control row; absorbing (no switch-offs). time_var 'time' is column 26 of data.long.sample.rds, which Table1.R drops; it equals the month factor's index 1..35 in every row (verified), so the FE structure is identical. Shipped data: random sample of the paper's panel (ReadMe.txt), 214 adopters + 3,790 never-adopters x 35 months = 140,140 rows, balanced, no duplicates, no missing outcomes; 9 adoption cohorts (months 13-21: 27, 16, 13, 26, 26, 16, 25, 31, 34 adopters); never-treated share 94.7% of customers; no always-treated. published_coef/se are the FULL-PANEL values from the authors' log (2 significant digits); subsample_* fields hold the shipped-sample estimates (authors' plm SE in subsample_twfe_raw_se). Not the authors' preferred estimate: they prefer rolling-entry matched pairs (Table 3, excluded as a matching estimator); Table 1 is the before-matching panel regression. The abstract reports no numbers; its qualitative claim (more purchases, more often, more items) concerns the same outcomes but rests on the matched analysis; the introduction is unavailable, so in_abstract_intro = false is unverified. Adoption is self-selected (quasi-experimental), so parallel trends between adopters and never-adopters is a strong assumption (pre-match covariates are imbalanced, Table 2 log).
